title: Grade 6 Math — Thu, Jun 12
description: Basic Geometry — Day 4 of 5: Drawing angles; angles in triangles
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The sum of all angles in a triangle is ___.
questions.explanation: The three interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180°.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 60° and 70°. What is the third angle?
Can a triangle have two right angles?
questions.explanation: Two right angles = 180°. The third angle would be 0°, which is impossible. No triangle can have two right angles.

questions.question: An equilateral triangle has three equal angles. What is each angle?
questions.explanation: Equilateral means all 3 angles are equal. 180° ÷ 3 = 60° each.

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has one 90° angle. The other two angles add up to ___.
questions.explanation: Total = 180°. 180° − 90° = 90°. The other two angles together make 90°.

questions.question: In a triangle, two angles are 45° each. What type of triangle is it?
questions.explanation: Two 45° angles; third = 180 − 45 − 45 = 90°. It has a right angle and two equal angles — right-angled isosceles.

questions.question: To draw an angle of 60° with a protractor, place the centre at the ___ of the angle.
questions.explanation: Place the centre (midpoint hole) of the protractor at the vertex — the point where the angle is formed.

questions.question: Which angle cannot exist in a triangle?
questions.explanation: Any single angle less than 180° can be in a triangle (as long as all three add to 180°). All three options can exist.

questions.question: A triangle has angles in the ratio 1:2:3. The largest angle is ___.
An obtuse triangle has ___.
options: No right angles and one obtuse angle
questions.explanation: An obtuse triangle has exactly one angle greater than 90°. Having two would exceed 180°.

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle are 80° and 60°. The triangle is ___.
questions.explanation: Third angle = 180 − 80 − 60 = 40°. All angles (40°, 60°, 80°) are less than 90° — acute triangle.

questions.question: If one angle of a triangle is 120°, the triangle is ___.
questions.explanation: 120° > 90°. The triangle has an obtuse angle, making it an obtuse triangle.

questions.question: When you use a protractor, which scale do you read — inner or outer?
options: It depends on the direction you drew the angle
questions.explanation: Protractors have two scales. Which one you use depends on which direction (clockwise or counter-clockwise) you measure from.

questions.question: The sum of all INTERIOR angles of a quadrilateral (4-sided figure) is ___.
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral can be split into 2 triangles. 2 × 180° = 360°.

questions.question: In a square, each interior angle is ___.
questions.explanation: A square has 4 equal angles. 360° ÷ 4 = 90° each.
